description: Deterministic Offline Symptom to Condition Mappings and Differential Assessment

conditions.name: Viral Upper Respiratory Tract Infection
missingInformation: Presence of yellow/green phlegm or blood in sputum
Ability to keep oral liquids down without vomiting
Recent exposure to known COVID-19 or influenza contacts
conditions.reasoning: Combination of fever with upper respiratory symptoms (cough, runny nose, or sore throat) without signs of lower respiratory compromise strongly aligns with a self-limiting viral upper respiratory infection.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Rest, maintain adequate oral hydration with boiled warm water and soups, warm saline gargling, monitor temperature. Consult primary care doctor if fever exceeds 102°F or lasts beyond 3 days.

conditions.name: Influenza-like Illness (ILI)
missingInformation: Sudden vs gradual onset of high fever and severe myalgia
Influenza vaccination history for current season
Underlying asthma, COPD, or diabetes
conditions.reasoning: Acute high fever accompanied by prominent generalized body aches, severe fatigue, and headache is classic presentation for influenza-like illness.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Strict bed rest, oral rehydration, isolate from vulnerable family members (elderly/infants). Doctor consultation advised for prescription fever antipyretics and clinical monitoring.

conditions.name: Acute Gastroenteritis / Acute Enteric Infection
missingInformation: Frequency of loose motions and vomiting episodes in past 24 hours
Presence of blood or mucus in stools
Urine frequency and color (checking for dehydration signs)
conditions.reasoning: Gastrointestinal symptoms with frequent loose stools, abdominal cramping, and nausea/vomiting indicate acute mucosal inflammation, commonly infectious or food/water contamination.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Start Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) solution immediately after every loose stool. Drink sip-by-sip. Do not withhold fluids. If signs of dehydration appear (dry tongue, no urine for 6 hours), visit PHC immediately.

conditions.name: Tension-Type Headache / Cephalea
missingInformation: Location of pain (unilateral vs band-like bilateral tension)
Sensitivity to bright light (photophobia) or loud sound
Neck stiffness or sudden 'thunderclap' onset
conditions.reasoning: Isolated headache without fever, neck rigidity, or focal neurological deficits commonly relates to tension, eye strain, dehydration, or stress.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Rest in a quiet, dark room, ensure adequate water intake, avoid prolonged screen or direct sunlight exposure. If accompanied by vomiting, visual aura, or neck stiffness, consult doctor.

conditions.name: Bronchial Asthma Exacerbation / Bronchospasm
missingInformation: Audible wheezing sound when breathing out
History of known asthma or prescribed inhaler use
SpO2 oxygen saturation level
conditions.reasoning: Breathlessness coupled with cough and chest tightness indicates lower airway narrowing or bronchospasm.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Use prescribed rescue reliever inhaler (e.g. Salbutamol) if previously diagnosed. Keep patient seated upright. If breathing does not ease within 10 minutes or pulse oximetry is under 93%, seek urgent emergency care.

conditions.name: Essential Hypertension / Blood Pressure Surge
missingInformation: Exact systolic and diastolic measurement numbers (e.g. 150/95)
Adherence to regular antihypertensive medicines (e.g. Amlodipine/Telmisartan)
Blurry vision or chest pressure
conditions.reasoning: Elevated blood pressure values with occipital headache or lightheadedness require evaluation for uncontrolled hypertension or medication non-compliance.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Rest calmly for 15 minutes and repeat BP reading. Do not suddenly double medication without doctor review. Visit local PHC or clinic for prescription titration.

conditions.name: Hyperglycemia / Diabetes Mellitus Exacerbation
missingInformation: Fasting vs post-prandial glucose reading in mg/dL
Increased thirst (polydipsia) or frequent urination (polyuria)
Current anti-diabetic medication or insulin adherence
conditions.reasoning: Reported elevated glucose levels with fatigue suggest glycemic dysregulation requiring dietary review and medical management.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Maintain hydration with plain water. Avoid sugary drinks and high-glycemic carbohydrates. Have fasting and PP blood sugar tested at PHC lab and review with physician.

conditions.name: Tropical Febrile Illness / Dengue Suspect
missingInformation: Pain behind the eyes (retro-orbital pain)
Skin rash, petechiae, or bleeding gums
Complete Blood Count (platelet count and hematocrit)
conditions.reasoning: High continuous fever accompanied by severe retro-orbital pain, bone-break myalgia, and profound weakness in endemic rural regions requires screening for vector-borne infections like dengue or chikungunya.
conditions.recommendedNextStep: Seek doctor consultation for CBC (platelet count) and dengue NS1/serology. Maintain high fluid intake. Avoid NSAIDs (aspirin, ibuprofen); only paracetamol under doctor instruction.
